learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn to divide a sentence into its two main components: the Subject (who/what) and the Predicate (the action or state).]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Every sentence is like a mini-movie! 🎬 It needs a star (the Subject) and some action (the Predicate). Let's learn how to spot the stars and the action in our sentences today!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The Subject is the part of the sentence that names the person, place, animal, or thing we are speaking about. It usually comes at the beginning of the sentence.
examples_or_templates: In 'The dog barked loudly', 'The dog' is the Subject.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The Predicate is the part of the sentence that tells us something about the Subject. It always contains the verb (the action or being word).
examples_or_templates: In 'The dog barked loudly', 'barked loudly' is the Predicate.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: In Imperative sentences (commands or requests), the Subject is usually not spoken or written. It is understood to be 'You'.
examples_or_templates: 'Sit down.' -> The hidden subject is '(You) sit down.'

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the Subject in this sentence: 'The bright yellow sun shone in the sky.'
❓ What is the hidden Subject in the sentence: 'Close the door!'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Underline the Subject and circle the Predicate: 'My best friend loves to eat pizza.'
subjective_practice.hint: Ask 'Who loves to eat pizza?' to find the subject.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Add a suitable Predicate to this Subject: 'The wild tiger _________.'
subjective_practice.hint: Think of an action a tiger does in the jungle.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Add a suitable Subject to this Predicate: '_________ won the first prize in the competition.'
subjective_practice.hint: Think of a person or a team name.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🧩 Sentence Match-Up
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write down 5 Subjects on five strips of paper, and 5 Predicates on another five strips. Mix them up and try to create the funniest valid sentences you can by drawing one of each!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Every complete sentence has two parts: a Subject and a Predicate.
⭐ The Subject tells us WHO or WHAT the sentence is about.
⭐ The Predicate tells us what the subject DOES or IS, and it always contains a verb.
